gh issue create --label ready-for-agent --title "tools, server, tui: the project proposal" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'\n## Source\n\n[docs/PLAN-phase6.md](https://github.com/stevewerme/aigentic/blob/main/docs/PLAN-phase6.md) — step 11 of [§10 Steps](https://github.com/stevewerme/aigentic/blob/main/docs/PLAN-phase6.md#10-steps-one-commit-each), with §9 "Proposal and switch" and §2's signatures. The plan is binding; read it before starting.\n\n## What to build\n\nMid-conversation, when a message belongs to another project, the model calls `suggest_project` before anything else in its turn. The actor appends `project_proposed`, pushes `AwaitingSwitch`, and pauses the turn. The client shows a switch-proposal block above the composer with the target project and the reason; `y` records the answer, performs the same switch `/project use` does, and runs the turn in the new project; `n` records the answer and runs the turn where it was. Every proposal and every answer lands in the log — that log is what a later classifier is trained and judged against, so it is kept from day one. The model's prefix lists the projects the user has a role in, one line each (the brief's first line once step 12's briefs exist; names and roots until then). Under `exec` a proposal is declined and logged. A switch request is refused while a turn runs.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] The model can call `suggest_project { project, reason }` first in a turn; the actor does not run it, it appends `project_proposed` and pauses the turn\n- [ ] `AwaitingSwitch` reaches the client as a block with the target and reason; `AnswerSwitch` records the answer in the log\n- [ ] `y` switches exactly as `/project use` does (role check, layers swapped, `ProjectSwitched` note, `Usage` push) and the turn runs in the new project; `n` runs the turn in the old one\n- [ ] A `SwitchProject` request is refused while the thread's turn is running\n- [ ] `exec` declines a proposal non-interactively, logs the answer, and says so\n- [ ] The prefix lists the user's projects with a one-line description each\n- [ ] The proposal log (project, reason, accepted) replays and projects correctly from an old log\n- [ ] `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test` pass\n\n## Blocked by\n\nNone (can start immediately; step 10's workspaces and `/project use` are landed).\nEOF\n)"

gh issue comment 7 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'\n## Design (from a dig through the code)\n\n**Interception, not execution.** `suggest_project` is a harness tool (`harness_tools.rs`): a spec the model sees, but the arm in `run_harness_tool` never runs it. Instead it appends `project_proposed` (`ProjectProposedPayload { project, reason, accepted: None }`), registers `Pending::Switch { call_id, project, reason }` in `Decisions`, fires `Signal::Waiting`, and parks on the oneshot with the cancel race — exactly the `ask_human` flow (`harness_tools.rs:181`), which is the solved-problem precedent for parking a running turn.\n\n**The answer performs the switch.** `Request::AnswerSwitch { thread, accept }` → session → `Mail::AnswerSwitch`. The wrinkle: `handle_running` is static and cannot touch the runtime (that is *why* `Mail::SwitchProject` is refused mid-turn, `actor.rs:754`), so the target's `ProjectContext` must be built in the session layer (as `ThreadTable::switch` does, `threads.rs:112`) and travel **through the answer channel**: `Answered::Switch { accept, by, ctx }`. The parked turn wakes holding `&mut self`, so it can itself call `set_project(ctx, by, observe)` — appending `project_switched`, pushing `Usage` — then append the answer event and return the tool result ("accepted; you are now in marketing (/root)" / "declined; continue here"). The turn loop continues and the *next model call* is already in the new project: layers, workdir, tools. "Runs the turn in the new project" needs no new control flow.\n\n**The answer in the log.** The plan gives one kind with `accepted: Option<bool>`, so two events of that kind: the proposal with `accepted: None`, the answer with `accepted: Some(bool)`, the answer's `parent_event` linking to the proposal, author = who answered (the `PermissionRequested`/`PermissionDecided` pair folded into one kind). The projection pairs them into (project, reason, accepted) rows — the classifier's training data.\n\n**The client.** `ThreadState::AwaitingSwitch { call_id, project, reason }` (peer of `AwaitingApproval`/`AwaitingHuman`), a `PromptBlock::Switch` above the composer, and `y`/`n` intercepted in `handle_line` like the approval block's `y/a/p/n` (`engine.rs:397`). Note: the plan §2's `Action::AnswerSwitch(bool)` keymap action never landed as such — step 7 chose typed lines, so this step follows the landed pattern.\n\n**The prefix.** A new `Prefix` field (peer of `participants`), from a new `ProjectContext` field: the user's projects, one line each (name and root until step 12's briefs exist), plus the call-it-first instruction.\n\n**exec.** The `Notice::State` match (`exec.rs:253`) gains an arm: print `[proposal declined: non-interactive]`, send `AnswerSwitch { accept: false }`.\n\nAlready in place from step 10: the switch itself (`SwitchProject`, `set_project`, `/project use`) and the mid-turn refusal — the refusal has code but no test.\n\n## Open questions\n\n1. **How the session learns the target.** `AnswerSwitch { thread, accept }` carries no project, but the ctx must be built session-side. Either the request also carries the project (the client knows it from the state; the actor verifies it matches the pending) — fewer round trips — or a pre-query mail asks the actor for the pending target, keeping the wire exactly as planned.\n2. **Not-first / sibling calls.** If `suggest_project` arrives alongside other calls in the same assistant message, the candidate rule (mirroring the interrupt path, `turn.rs:284`): remaining calls get synthetic "not run: the turn paused for a project proposal" results so the log stays projectable.\n3. **A proposal for a project the user cannot `write` in.** Refuse the accept at the session (role check, like `SwitchProject`) — and the tool result tells the model so it can continue in place.\n\nProposed defaults: carry the project in the request and verify server-side; synthetic results for sibling calls; refuse-with-explanation on role.\n\n## Tests\n\nMirroring `crates/server/tests/switch.rs` with a scripted provider: propose→accept (proposal + answer + `project_switched` in the log, turn continues in the new root); propose→decline; exec auto-decline; the prefix lists projects; the mid-turn `SwitchProject` refusal (currently untested); a `log` fixture test that old logs replay and the proposal pair projects.\nEOF\n)"

cat >> crates/tui/src/app/mod.rs <<'EOF'\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::app::menu::{Menu, Pick};\n    use aigentic_runtime::aigentic_core::{RiskClass, ToolCall};\n    use serde_json::json;\n\n    fn text(lines: &[Line<'_>]) -> Vec<String> {\n        lines\n            .iter()\n            .map(|l| l.spans.iter().map(|s| s.content.as_ref()).collect())\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    fn bash(command: &str) -> ToolCall {\n        ToolCall {\n            id: "c1".into(),\n            name: "bash".into(),\n            args: json!({"command": command}),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn approval(command: &str) -> Menu {\n        Menu::permission(\n            &bash(command),\n            RiskClass::Exec,\n            "class exec: anything else in a shell",\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// The screen the issue draws: the header in plain words, the\n    /// command in full under it, the rows numbered with the selected one\n    /// marked, and Esc named on the deny.\n    #[test]\n    fn the_approval_menu_renders_as_the_issue_draws_it() {\n        let menu = approval("sed -n '/^## 4\\\\./,/^## 10\\\\./p' docs/PLAN-phase6.md");\n        let lines = text(&block_lines(&menu, 76));\n        assert_eq!(\n            lines,\n            vec![\n                " Run this command?",\n                "   sed -n '/^## 4\\\\./,/^## 10\\\\./p' docs/PLAN-phase6.md",\n                " ❯ 1. Yes",\n                "   2. Yes, and don't ask again for `sed -n` in this project",\n                format!(\n                    "   3. No, and tell the agent why{}(esc)",\n                    " ".repeat(39)\n                ),\n            ]\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// The full text wraps and hangs; nothing is cut to one line, and a\n    /// very long one is capped head and tail, as tool output is.\n    #[test]\n    fn the_body_wraps_and_a_very_long_one_is_capped() {\n        let menu = approval("grep pattern crates/tui/src");\n        let lines = text(&block_lines(&menu, 40));\n        assert_eq!(\n            lines,\n            vec![\n                " Run this command?",\n                "   grep pattern crates/tui/src",\n                " ❯ 1. Yes",\n                "   2. Yes, and don't ask again for",\n                "      `grep pattern` in this project",\n                format!("   3. No, and tell the agent why   (esc)"),\n            ]\n        );\n        let command = (1..=12)\n            .map(|i| format!("line{i}"))\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            .join("\\n");\n        let menu = approval(&command);\n        let lines = text(&block_lines(&menu, 40));\n        assert_eq!(\n            lines[..9],\n            [\n                " Run this command?",\n                "   line1",\n                "   line2",\n                "   line3",\n                "   line4",\n                "   line5",\n                "   … 5 rows",\n                "   line11",\n                "   line12",\n            ]\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// A question in the pre-options shape: the question, and the\n    /// composer takes the answer. A rule's own reason is a dim line\n    /// under the options; a class-generated one is not shown.\n    #[test]\n    fn a_question_is_the_question_and_a_rules_reason_stays() {\n        let menu = Menu::question("which colour?");\n        assert_eq!(\n            text(&block_lines(&menu, 40)),\n            vec![" which colour?", "   type the answer"]\n        );\n        let call = ToolCall {\n            id: "c2".into(),\n            name: "mcp.docs.search".into(),\n            args: json!({"query": "phase 6"}),\n        };\n        let menu = Menu::permission(&call, RiskClass::Network, "mcp.docs: the plan says ask");\n        let lines = block_lines(&menu, 76);\n        let last = lines.last().unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(\n            last.spans.iter().map(|s| s.content.as_ref()).collect::<String>(),\n            "   mcp.docs: the plan says ask"\n        );\n        assert!(last.spans[0].style.modifier.contains(Modifier::DIM));\n        assert!(menu.note.is_some());\n        let menu = approval("rm -rf build");\n        assert_eq!(menu.note, None, "the class reason adds nothing");\n    }\n}\nEOF\necho done

Red · the warm one",\n            "  2. Green",\n            "  3. Other: type your own",\n        ]\n    );\n    // A digit picks a row; the answer is the contribution, headed.\n    assert_eq!(\n        menu.key(&key(KeyCode::Char('2'), KeyModifiers::NONE), true, true),\n        answer("colour: Green")\n    );\n    // The engine applies it: the next question shows, multi this time.\n    assert_eq!(menu.answer("colour: Green"), None);\n    assert_eq!(menu.title, "Which tests?");\n    assert!(menu.multi);\n    assert_eq!(menu.note.as_deref(), Some("space toggles · enter sends · a pipe: `1 2`"));\n    // Space toggles the selected row; digits toggle too.\n    assert_eq!(\n        menu.key(&key(KeyCode::Char(' '), KeyModifiers::NONE), true, true),\n        Keyed::Used\n    );\n    assert!(menu.picked[0]);\n    assert_eq!(\n        menu.key(&key(KeyCode::Char('2'), KeyModifiers::NONE), true, true),\n        Keyed::Used\n    );\n    assert!(menu.picked[1]);\n    // Enter submits the picked rows.\n    assert_eq!(\n        menu.key(&key(KeyCode::Enter, KeyModifiers::NONE), true, true),\n        answer("unit, integration")\n    );\n    assert_eq!(menu.answer("unit, integration"), None);\n    // A question without options: the composer takes it, free text.\n    assert_eq!(menu.title, "Ship it?");\n    assert!(menu.rows.is_empty());\n    assert_eq!(menu.line("yes, friday"), Some(answer("yes, friday")));\n    assert_eq!(\n        menu.answer("yes, friday").unwrap(),\n        "colour: Green\\nunit, integration\\nyes, friday"\n    );\n}\n\n/// A pipe reads numbers for a question: one number picks a row,\n/// several (space or comma separated) pick several when the question\n/// allows it, and anything else is free text.\n#[test]\nfn a_pipe_answers_a_question_by_number_or_text() {\n    let mut menu = Menu::asking(asked());\n    assert_eq!(menu.line("1"), Some(answer("colour: Red")));\n    assert_eq!(menu.line("red please"), Some(answer("colour: red please")));\n    assert_eq!(menu.answer("colour: red please"), None);\n    assert_eq!(menu.line("2 1"), Some(answer("integration, unit")));\n    assert_eq!(menu.line("2,1"), Some(answer("integration, unit")));\n    assert_eq!(menu.line("9"), Some(answer("9")), "a number past the rows is free text");\n    assert_eq!(menu.line("both please"), Some(answer("both please")));\n    assert_eq!(\n        menu.answer("both please"),\n        Some("colour: red please\\nboth please".to_owned()),\n        "one go: the whole call in one answer"\n    );\n    // A number is not an answer while a draft is being typed: the\n    // composer is the free-text answer.\n    let menu = Menu::asking(asked());\n    assert_eq!(\n        menu.key(&key(KeyCode::Char('1'), KeyModifiers::NONE), false, true),\n        Keyed::Passed\n    );\n    // Picking Other hands the composer to the question.\n    let mut menu = Menu::asking(asked());\n    assert_eq!(\n        menu.key(&key(KeyCode::Char('3'), KeyModifiers::NONE), true, true),\n        Keyed::Text\n    );\n    assert_eq!(menu.free_text("magenta"), "colour: magenta");\n}\nEOF\ncargo test -p aigentic-tui menu:: 2>&1 | grep -E "^error" -A6 | head -30

A prompt answered\n    /// elsewhere first is gone; the text goes nowhere.\n    pub async fn prompt_text(&mut self, reason: Option<String>, out: &mut dyn Printer) {\n        if self.menu().is_none() {\n            return;\n        }\n        if self\n            .menu\n            .as_ref()\n            .is_some_and(|m| m.kind == Kind::Permission)\n        {\n            let echo = match &reason {\n                Some(r) => format!("\\\\u{21b3} No: {r}"),\n                None => "\\\\u{21b3} No".into(),\n            };\n            out.line(&echo);\n            self.decide(false, false, None, reason, out).await;\n        }\n    }\n'''\n\nnew = '''    /// A key while the menu is up: the selection, the digits, the hidden\n    /// accelerators and Enter, sending the decision with the echo of\n    /// what was chosen. `composer_empty` and `settled` as `Menu::key`\n    /// takes them. `Text` says the composer should take the prompt's\n    /// text.\n    pub async fn menu_key(\n        &mut self,\n        key: &crossterm::event::KeyEvent,\n        composer_empty: bool,\n        settled: bool,\n        out: &mut dyn Printer,\n    ) -> MenuKey {\n        if self.prompted.is_none() {\n            return MenuKey::Passed;\n        }\n        let Some(menu) = self.menu.as_mut() else {\n            return MenuKey::Passed;\n        };\n        match menu.key(key, composer_empty, settled) {\n            Keyed::Passed => MenuKey::Passed,\n            Keyed::Text => MenuKey::Text,\n            Keyed::Used => MenuKey::Used,\n            keyed @ (Keyed::Decide { .. } | Keyed::Answer { .. }) => {\n                self.apply(keyed, out).await;\n                MenuKey::Used\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// What the menu came to: a decision, or an answer to the current\n    /// question — echoed, and sent when it was the last.\n    async fn apply(&mut self, keyed: Keyed, out: &mut dyn Printer) {\n        match keyed {\n            Keyed::Decide {\n                pick,\n                reason,\n                echo,\n            } => {\n                out.line(&echo);\n                match pick {\n                    Pick::Allow { session, prefix } => {\n                        self.decide(true, session, prefix, reason, out).await;\n                    }\n                    Pick::Deny => {\n                        self.decide(false, false, None, reason, out).await;\n                    }\n                    Pick::Answer | Pick::Other => {}\n                }\n            }\n            Keyed::Answer { text, echo } => {\n                out.line(&echo);\n                if let Some(menu) = self.menu.as_mut()\n                    && let Some(all) = menu.answer(&text)\n                {\n                    self.answer_human(all, out).await;\n                }\n            }\n            Keyed::Passed | Keyed::Used | Keyed::Text => {}\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Send the composed answer to the question this client is prompted\n    /// for.\n    async fn answer_human(&mut self, text: String, out: &mut dyn Printer) {\n        let Some(call_id) = self.prompted.clone() else {\n            return;\n        };\n        let r = self\n            .request(Request::AnswerHuman {\n                thread: self.thread,\n                call_id,\n                text,\n            })\n            .await;\n        self.answered(r, out);\n    }\n\n    /// The composer's text for the prompt, Enter on its text input: a\n    /// deny's reason, with none when it was empty, or a question's\n    /// free-text answer, headed like any other. A prompt answered\n    /// elsewhere first is gone; the text goes nowhere.\n    pub async fn prompt_text(&mut self, text: Option<String>, out: &mut dyn Printer) {\n        if self.menu().is_none() {\n            return;\n        }\n        match self.menu.as_ref().map(|m| m.kind) {\n            Some(Kind::Permission) => {\n                let echo = match &text {\n                    Some(r) => format!("\\\\u{21b3} No: {r}"),\n                    None => "\\\\u{21b3} No".into(),\n                };\n                out.line(&echo);\n                self.decide(false, false, None, text, out).await;\n            }\n            Some(Kind::Question) => {\n                if let Some(t) = text.map(|t| t.trim().to_owned()).filter(|t| !t.is_empty()) {\n                    let contribution = self\n                        .menu\n                        .as_ref()\n                        .map(|m| m.free_text(&t))\n                        .unwrap_or(t.clone());\n                    out.line(&format!("\\\\u{21b3} {contribution}"));\n                    if let Some(menu) = self.menu.as_mut()\n                        && let Some(all) = menu.answer(&contribution)\n                    {\n                        self.answer_human(all, out).await;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            None => {}\n        }\n    }\n'''\nassert old in s, "old block not found"\ns = s.replace(old, new)\nopen(p, 'w').write(s)\nprint('ok')\nEOF

cat >> crates/runtime/tests/ask_human.rs <<'EOF'\n\n/// A log the old binary wrote — a single-question `ask_human`, answered\n/// — replays: the runtime continues from the recorded answer, the\n/// model's context carries it, and nothing re-parses the call (event\n/// kinds are added, never changed; AGENTS.md).\n#[tokio::test]\nasync fn an_old_log_with_the_single_question_shape_replays() {\n    use aigentic_core::ContentBlock;\n    use aigentic_log::{AssistantMessagePayload, NewEvent, PolicyRecord, ToolResultPayload, UserMessagePayload, TurnEndedPayload};\n\n    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();\n    let mut log = ThreadLog::open(dir.path(), ulid::Ulid::generate()).unwrap();\n    let ev = |kind, author, payload| NewEvent {\n        kind,\n        author,\n        payload,\n        parent_event: None,\n    };\n    let asked = ToolCall {\n        id: "q1".into(),\n        name: "ask_human".into(),\n        args: json!({"question": "which colour?"}),\n    };\n    let assistant = ev(\n        EventKind::AssistantMessage,\n        Author::Agent(aigentic_core::AgentId("worker".into())),\n        serde_json::to_value(AssistantMessagePayload {\n            blocks: vec![ContentBlock::ToolCall(asked)],\n            usage: None,\n        })\n        .unwrap(),\n    );\n    let answered = ev(\n        EventKind::ToolResult,\n        steve(),\n        serde_json::to_value(ToolResultPayload::new(\n            aigentic_core::ToolResult {\n                id: "q1".into(),\n                content: "blue".into(),\n                is_error: false,\n            },\n            PolicyRecord::rule("class safe", aigentic_policy::Decision::Allow),\n        ))\n        .unwrap(),\n    );\n    let parent = log.append(assistant).unwrap().id;\n    let answered = NewEvent {\n        parent_event: Some(parent),\n        ..answered\n    };\n    for e in [\n        ev(\n            EventKind::UserMessage,\n            steve(),\n            serde_json::to_value(UserMessagePayload::new(vec![ContentBlock::Text("start".into())]))\n                .unwrap(),\n        ),\n        answered,\n        ev(\n            EventKind::TurnEnded,\n            Author::Agent(aigentic_core::AgentId("worker".into())),\n            serde_json::to_value(TurnEndedPayload::new(ASKED_HUMAN)).unwrap(),\n        ),\n    ] {\n        log.append(e).unwrap();\n    }\n    let harness = common::harness_with_log(\n        vec![vec![text("done"), done("stop")]],\n        None,\n        dir,\n        log,\n    );\n    assert!(harness.runtime.awaiting_continuation().unwrap());\n    let outcome = harness\n        .runtime\n        .continue_turn(&mut |_| {})\n        .await\n        .unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(outcome.reason, "done");\n    // The continuation's context carries the recorded answer, not a\n    // re-asked question.\n    let seen = harness.seen.lock().unwrap();\n    let carried = seen.iter().any(|msgs| {\n        msgs.iter().any(|m| {\n            m.blocks.iter().any(|b| match b {\n                ContentBlock::ToolResult(r) => r.content == "blue",\n                _ => false,\n            })\n        })\n    });\n    assert!(carried, "the old log's answer is in the context");\n}\nEOF\ncargo test -p aigentic-runtime --test ask_human 2>&1 | grep -E "^error" -A8 | head git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'\nlog, runtime: evict stale results and edit arguments inside a turn\n\nNothing shrank a context inside a turn: compaction triggers at a\nfraction of the window (734k on GLM 5.3) and only covers turns older\nthan the last keep_turns, so the #13 build thread grew to 285k tokens\nover 224 calls and paid 43M input tokens for it. 55% of it was the\nmodel's own edit_file old/new strings and 39% consumed tool results.\n\nA new context_evicted event records how far a sweep reached. The\nprojection applies it inside that turn only: a tool result older than\nthe boundary becomes [result of <tool> <short args> · <n> lines ·\ndropped from context; re-run it if you need it again], and a\nsuccessful edit_file/write_file call's arguments become [edited\n<path>: -a/+b lines], the diff shape read off its result before that\ntoo is stubbed. Failed results and the last result of each distinct\ntool stay. Nothing is deleted and old logs replay unchanged: without\nthe event nothing is stubbed.\n\nThe sweep runs beside compaction at the top of the loop, at iteration\nboundaries only, and moves the boundary whole blocks of 8 calls at a\ntime so the provider's prompt cache keeps a stable prefix between\nsweeps; keep_last_calls (12 by default, [compaction] in aigentic.toml\nand the profile's [profiles.X.compaction]) is how many calls of the\nrunning turn stay in full. A 200-call turn with 30k reads, writes and\nedits stays under 128k tokens on every call (#30).\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)" && git log --oneline -1
